texts.facts: The sample was found to contain 1.2% moisture and thus adulterated as the maximum moisture percentage prescribed was 0.5%. (2 of 3) [CRLR-420/2017] 3. It is contended that charge-sheet was filed against petitioner and his father Amolak Chand his father expired during pendency of the trial and the Court proceeded against the present petitioner. The prayer of the petitioner was allowed by the Court on 28.11.1990 and directions were given for sending the sample to Central Food Laboratory. was submitted by the Central Food Laboratory.
texts.arguments: 2. It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that sample of Ghee was taken from the shop M/s. Amolak Chand Tara Chand situated at Ghee Mandi, Madar Gate, Ajmer on 05.02.1990. 4. It is contended that the petitioner moved the Court for sending the sample to Central Food Laboratory. 5. It is contended by the counsel that the sample was sent laboratory to Central Food Laboratory after twenty years of the date of taking of sample and as such there was no justification for the Court below to place reliance on the report given by Central Food Laboratory. It is also contended that the report of the Central Food Laboratory was not put to the petitioner under Section 313 Cr.P.C. and therefore placing conviction on the said report is perse illegal. 7. Public Prosecutor has opposed the revision petition her contention is that the sample was found to be adulterated. 8.
